title: ENEA and partners test a machine-learning system to forecast heatwave-driven grid failures in Italy
summary: ENEA and university partners tested grid-failure forecasts using past faults, weather, and energy flows. Their May 18, 2023 report describes held-out testing but no avoided outage.
account: ENEA, Politecnico di Bari, and Università Roma Tre tested machine-learning forecasts of heatwave-related failures in a large distribution grid in southern Italy. ENEA’s May 18, 2023 announcement says that training used failures from 2015 to 2020, temperature, humidity, and energy flows, followed by tests on unseen inputs. Researchers proposed that operators use the forecasts for corrective maintenance. The inspected announcement reports neither a named utility deployment nor an avoided outage.
purpose: The system was built to forecast heatwave-related failures on electricity networks so operators can act in advance. The record documents development and testing only.
system: ENEA machine-learning heatwave grid-failure forecasting model
developer: ENEA with Politecnico di Bari and Università Roma Tre
taxonomy_note: The research announcement describes preventing heatwave-induced grid failures, with no deployment or avoided outage documented.

ratings.reason: No avoided blackout or deployment is documented.
No grid operator use is documented.

ai_role.statement: Machine learning predicted grid failures from historical failures, weather, and energy flows. Researchers tested it on unseen inputs, but the inspected announcement gives no numeric accuracy or evidence that an operator used the forecasts to prevent an outage.
